tools/facts.py: Not a bare reach claim. Every flagged count is either a failure message printed as the command exits non-zero ('<n> of <m> file(s) could not be read' states its population; '<n> malformed record(s)' and '<n> records ... disagree' name the defect, and the run is refused), or validate's JSON. There 'records' counts the records parsed from the input the caller chose: the fixed home files by default, or with --records a file the caller named on the command line, which the output does not echo. Next to it, 'errors' names every line that held a record start and did not parse, so each record line is either counted or named, and validate exits 1 when any is named. Lines 298, 344 and 447 are detector false positives (a regex, an any() over name parts, a module name). kb-facts-1127, 2026-11-27, org 67 ruling; corrected per Codex narrow 25.F1.
